cards.english: What is your name?
Do you speak English?
cards.existing: Always lowercase: `по-французски` (po-frantsuzski) not `По-Французски`. And no space – the hyphen sticks it to the adjective stem.

cards.english: Who wrote this book?
cards.existing: Every Russian verb comes in a pair: imperfective (process) and perfective (result). `Читать` (be reading) vs `прочитать` (have read). Pick by situation.

cards.english: The brother often buys groceries.
The discount is fifteen percent.
Birds sing beautifully in spring.
cards.existing: These plural endings also appear when speaking about an unspecified group: `говорят, что...` = 'they say that...' (people in general).

cards.english: Has he really already left?
May I open the window?
cards.existing: `Можно` (one can/may) and `нельзя` (one can't/may not) are impersonal: `Здесь можно курить?` (Can one smoke here?). No subject needed.

cards.english: Where can I buy souvenirs?
cards.existing: `Надо` (Nado) and `нужно` = 'need to / should'. Person goes dative: `Мне надо идти` (I need to go – literally 'to-me necessary to-go'). The 'subject' is in dative.

cards.english: This is my brother's house.
Dad always reads books.
cards.existing: `Каждый` (every) and `весь` (all/whole) act like adjectives – match gender, number, case. `Каждый день` (m, nom), `всю ночь` (f, acc).

cards.english: When does the next bus leave?
She plans to start a vegetable garden.
cards.existing: You can guess conjugation from the infinitive. `-ить (it')` and most `-еть` → II conjugation (-ишь/-ит/…). Most `-ать/-ять/-овать` → I conjugation (-ешь/-ет/…).

cards.english: May I have a glass of water?
cards.existing: `Должен/должна/должно/должны` (must/should) does agree with the subject in gender/number: `Я должен идти` (m), `она должна идти` (f).

cards.english: I saw the work through to the end.
She cannot come today.
Hi, let's meet after work.
We read about ancient history.
We don't need your help.
cards.existing: Dative pronouns: мне (mne)/тебе/ему/ей/нам/вам/им. Used for the recipient ('to me'), age ('I'm 20 = мне 20'), and impersonal feeling ('I'm cold = мне холодно').

cards.english: We have no available seats.
cards.existing: Past: `у меня была книга` (u menya byla kniga) (I had a book). Future: `у меня будет книга` (I will have a book). `Был/была/было/были` agrees with the thing owned.

cards.english: My friend has a country house.

cards.target: Сосед скоро будет работать в офисе.
cards.english: The neighbor will work in the office soon.
The girl often works in the office.
Which movie do you want to watch?
cards.existing: `Почему` (why-cause) vs `зачем` (why-purpose). `Почему ты плачешь?` (why are you crying – what caused this?) vs `зачем ты пришёл?` (why did you come – what for?).

cards.english: There's nowhere to walk in this city.

cards.target: Мы понимаем друг друга без слов.
cards.english: We understand each other without words.

cards.target: Я работаю в офисе каждый день.
cards.english: I work in the office every day.

cards.target: Медсестра ездит на работу после обеда.
cards.english: The nurse commutes to work after lunch.

cards.target: Не могли бы вы помочь мне с чемоданом?
cards.english: Could you help me with my suitcase?
Six hours of work is tiring.
The musician usually helps a friend.
Is it possible to change rooms?
cards.existing: `Можно` (one can/may) and `нельзя` (one can't/may not) are impersonal: `Здесь можно курить?` (Can one smoke here?). No subject needed.

cards.english: There are eleven cars in the parking lot.
How do I get to the metro station?
cards.existing: `Где` vs `куда` vs `откуда`: location vs destination vs origin. `Где ты?` (Where are you?) vs `куда ты идёшь?` (Where are you going?). English uses 'where' for both.

cards.english: How many people will come to the party?
There are always many people at the airport.
He is not used to getting up early.
At the dacha there is a small vegetable garden.
The musician always commutes to work.
The chef rarely works in the office.
There are thirty students in our class.
Behind the school there is a sports field.

cards.target: Мы вернёмся через неделю, в воскресенье.
cards.english: We will return in a week on Sunday.

cards.target: Сестра часто бегает по утрам в парке.
cards.english: My sister often runs in the park in the mornings.

cards.target: Он ездит на работу на метро.
cards.english: He commutes to work by metro.

cards.target: На работе у него много обязанностей.
cards.english: He has many responsibilities at work.

cards.target: Инженер стирал одежду на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: The engineer washed clothes last week.

cards.target: Продавец мыл посуду на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: The salesman washed the dishes last week.

cards.target: Девятнадцатого мая у меня день рождения.
cards.english: My birthday is on the nineteenth of May.

cards.existing: If it answers 'whom?' and is a living being, use the genitive-style ending: `студента` (studenta), `мужчину`. For things, accusative = nominative for masc inanimate.

cards.target: Продавец ездил на работу на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: The salesman commuted to work last week.
cards.existing: `Я иду в школу` (going right now, single trip) vs `я хожу в школу` (I attend school, regularly). Same English 'go', two Russian verbs.

cards.target: Мы планируем посетить Эрмитаж на этих выходных.
cards.english: We plan to visit the Hermitage this weekend.

cards.target: На прошлой неделе мама по утрам бегала в парке.
cards.english: Last week mom ran in the park in the mornings.
Smoking is not allowed here.
cards.existing: `Должен/должна/должно/должны` (must/should) does agree with the subject in gender/number: `Я должен идти` (m), `она должна идти` (f).

cards.english: Who is the eldest among you?
cards.existing: `Почему` (why-cause) vs `зачем` (why-purpose). `Почему ты плачешь?` (why are you crying – what caused this?) vs `зачем ты пришёл?` (why did you come – what for?).

cards.target: Студенты сдают экзамены в конце семестра.
